groups.title: Library app — key information
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

parts.context: A librarian introduces a new library app to students.

transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'm Mr Jones, the senior librarian, and I'm delighted to introduce our new library app, which will replace the old online system from the beginning of next month.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: I've been working in libraries for a very long time, and I can honestly say that this is the biggest change I have seen. We've worked closely with the IT department and a group of students to make sure that it does what you need.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: Why are we changing? Well, we did a survey last year, and the main complaint was that the old system was slow and difficult to use on a phone. Students asked for something simpler, and this is the result.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: To log in, you just use your student number and the same password you use for the university email. There's no need to create a new account, which saves a lot of time.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: Once you are in, you can search the whole catalogue and renew your books. You can renew each book up to three times, as long as nobody else has reserved it. After that, you must bring it back.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: The renewal system is also much clearer than before. The app shows the new due date immediately, so you don't have to guess, and you can see all of your current loans on one screen.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: If a book is out on loan, you can reserve it. When it comes back, you receive a message, and the book is kept for you at the lockers by the main entrance. You don't need to ask at the desk.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: The feature that students have liked most in our tests is the interactive map of the study rooms. It shows which rooms are free right now, so you don't waste time walking around the building.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: You can also book a study room directly in the app. Each student can book a room for a maximum of two hours a day, so that everyone has a fair chance, and you can book up to seven days ahead.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: When you book, you receive a confirmation, and if you don't arrive within fifteen minutes, the room is released for other students. This rule might seem strict, but it stops people from booking rooms and not using them.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: The app sends notifications, too. You'll get a reminder three days before a book is due, and a second one on the day itself. This should help to avoid fines, which are currently fifty pence a day.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: Printing is also easier. You can pay with your phone, and each page costs ten pence. Previously, you needed a separate card and had to queue at the machine.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: We have also added a feature that tells you how busy the library is, which many of you will find useful during the exam period, when seats can be hard to find.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: The app is available for both Android and iPhone, and you can download it from the usual stores. If you have any problems, please contact the IT desk, which is on the ground floor.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES

transcript.text: I'd like to thank the students who tested the app for us. Their comments were extremely useful. Now, if you have your phones with you, let's try it together.
transcript.speaker: MR JONES
